intro: Hi! So far you've used am, is and are for now. In this lesson you'll talk about the past with was and were: where you were yesterday, how your weekend was, and who wasn't at the meeting. Warm-up: where were you last night? Try 'I was at home.'
teachingNotes: Indonesian doesn't change the verb for time: 'Kemarin saya sakit' uses the same words as today, only 'kemarin' shows the past. English changes the verb: am/is → was, are → were. The #1 error is *'Yesterday I am sick'; whenever the learner uses yesterday, last night, last week or last year, check that the verb is was/were.

was goes with I, he, she, it (one person or thing); were goes with you (one person or many), we and they. Stress *'They was at home' and *'You was late': two names (Rina and Budi) = they → were. Explain why 'you were' for one person: 'you' always takes 'are' (you are), and are → were. Also point out that 'they' covers things (the rooms, my shoes), while Indonesian 'mereka' is only for people, so learners pick 'was' for plural things.
Negatives: was not → wasn't, were not → weren't. Just add not after was/were; never *'not was' or *'didn't was'. In speech was and were are usually weak (/wəz/, /wə/); wasn't and weren't are strong.

Questions: put Was/Were before the subject (Were you at school yesterday?). Indonesian speakers often keep statement order and only raise their voice: *'You were at school yesterday?'. Short answers repeat was/were: Yes, I was. / No, they weren't. A 'Were you…?' question is answered with I: Yes, I was.

Limits: don't teach the past simple of other verbs (went, ate, did), there was/there were, or the past continuous yet. Fixed chunks are fine: I was born in…, How was your weekend? — It was great. No years (not taught yet): use yesterday, last week, last year, on Sunday. 'I was born in …' needs explaining: Indonesian 'saya lahir' has no extra word, so learners say *'I born' or *'I am born'; treat 'was born' as a fixed phrase.

keyPoints.title: was / were in positive sentences
keyPoints.explanation: Past of am/is → was (I, he, she, it). Past of are → were (you, we, they). 'you' takes were even for one person, because it's 'you are' now. 'they' is also for things (the rooms were …). Use them with past times like yesterday, last night, last week.

examples.en: I was at the office yesterday.
My friends were at the warung last night.

id.title: was / were dalam kalimat positif
id.explanation: Bentuk lampau dari am/is → was (I, he, she, it). Bentuk lampau dari are → were (you, we, they). 'you' memakai were walaupun untuk satu orang, karena sekarangnya 'you are'. 'they' juga dipakai untuk benda (the rooms were …). Pakai bersama kata waktu lampau seperti yesterday, last night, last week.

keyPoints.title: Negative: wasn't / weren't
keyPoints.explanation: Add not after was/were: was not → wasn't, were not → weren't. No other word is needed.

examples.en: She wasn't at school on Monday.
examples.id: Dia (perempuan) tidak masuk sekolah hari Senin.

id.title: Kalimat negatif: wasn't / weren't
id.explanation: Tambahkan not setelah was/were: was not → wasn't, were not → weren't. Tidak perlu kata lain.

keyPoints.title: Was / Were questions and short answers
keyPoints.explanation: Put was/were before the subject: Was he…? Were you…? Short answers repeat was/were: Yes, he was. / No, I wasn't.

examples.en: Was the film good? — Yes, it was.
Were you tired? — No, I wasn't.

id.title: Pertanyaan dengan Was / Were dan jawaban singkat
id.explanation: Taruh was/were sebelum subjek (siapa yang dibicarakan): Was he…? Were you…? Jawaban singkat mengulang was/were: Yes, he was. / No, I wasn't.

guidedPractice.prompt: Complete with was or were: I ___ tired last night.
Complete with was or were: My friends ___ at the warung at 7 p.m. yesterday.
Make it negative: I was hungry this morning.
expected: i was not hungry this morning

guidedPractice.prompt: Make a question: She was at the bank yesterday.
expected: was she at the bank yesterday

independentPractice.prompt: Translate: Mereka tidak di sekolah hari Jumat.
expected: they weren't at school on friday
they were not at school on friday
on friday they weren't at school
on friday they were not at school

independentPractice.prompt: Answer with a short answer (no): Was it hot in Jakarta yesterday?

assessment.prompt: Complete with was or were: Yesterday Budi ___ at the office all day.

assessment.rubric: Needs 'were'. 'we are in Bandung yesterday' = 30. 'we was' = 40. Missing verb = 20. 'at Bandung' = 80.

assessment.prompt: Make it negative: The shop was open on Sunday.
acceptableAnswers: the shop wasn't open on sunday
the shop was not open on sunday
assessment.rubric: Correct: The shop wasn't / was not open on Sunday. 'weren't' = 40. 'isn't' = 30. 'didn't open' = 30.

assessment.prompt: Make a question: Your parents were at home last night.
acceptableAnswers: were your parents at home last night
assessment.rubric: Correct: Were your parents at home last night? Statement order with a question mark = 20. 'Was your parents' = 40.

assessment.prompt: Listen. Give a short YES answer.
assessment.listen: Was your sister at the wedding on Sunday?
assessment.rubric: Correct: Yes, she was. 'Yes, he was' = 50 (wrong person). 'Yes, I was' = 40. 'Yes' alone = 40. 'Yes, she is' = 30.

assessment.prompt: Give a short NEGATIVE answer: Were they late for the meeting?
assessment.rubric: Correct: No, they weren't. 'No, they wasn't' = 40. 'No, they aren't' = 30. 'No' alone = 40.

blocks.text: Indonesian says *Saya di rumah* with no extra word, but English needs **am / is / are**: *I am at home*. For the past, these words change: **am** and **is** become **was**, and **are** becomes **were**. So: **I was**, **he/she/it was**, but **you were**, **we were**, **they were**. Remember: **you** takes **were** even for one person. Why? Because *you* always goes with *are* (*you are*), and *are* becomes *were*.

id.text: Bahasa Indonesia bilang *Saya di rumah* tanpa kata tambahan, tapi bahasa Inggris butuh **am / is / are**: *I am at home*. Untuk masa lalu, kata-kata ini berubah: **am** dan **is** menjadi **was**, dan **are** menjadi **were**. Jadi: **I was**, **he/she/it was**, tapi **you were**, **we were**, **they were**. Ingat: **you** memakai **were**, walaupun hanya satu orang. Kenapa? Karena *you* selalu berpasangan dengan *are* (*you are*), dan *are* menjadi *were*.

rows.en: I am at home. → I was at home.
rows.id: Saya di rumah. → Tadi saya di rumah.

rows.en: She is happy. → She was happy.
They are in Bali. → They were in Bali.
rows.id: Mereka di Bali. → Mereka (waktu itu) di Bali.

blocks.text: In Indonesian only the time word changes: *Kemarin saya sakit*. In English the verb changes too: **Yesterday I was sick**, not 'Yesterday I am sick'. The time word and was/were work as a team: if you say *yesterday*, say *was/were*.

id.text: Dalam bahasa Indonesia hanya kata waktunya yang berubah: *Kemarin saya sakit*. Dalam bahasa Inggris kata kerjanya juga berubah: **Yesterday I was sick**, bukan 'Yesterday I am sick'. Kata waktu dan was/were selalu berpasangan: kalau kamu bilang *yesterday*, pakai *was/were*.

blocks.prompt: My brother ___ in Bali last week.
blocks.explain: My brother = he, and last week is the past → was.

id.explain: My brother = he, dan last week itu masa lalu → was.
id.prompt: Lengkapi: My brother ___ in Bali last week.

blocks.text: These words tell you the sentence is about the past, so use **was/were**: **yesterday** (kemarin), **last night** (tadi malam / semalam), **last week** (minggu lalu), **last year** (tahun lalu), **on Sunday** (hari Minggu; with was/were it means the Sunday that has passed). They can go at the end or at the start: *I was busy yesterday.* / *Yesterday I was busy.*

id.text: Kata-kata ini menunjukkan bahwa kalimatnya tentang masa lalu, jadi pakai **was/were**: **yesterday** (kemarin), **last night** (tadi malam / semalam), **last week** (minggu lalu), **last year** (tahun lalu), **on Sunday** (hari Minggu; dengan was/were artinya hari Minggu yang sudah lewat). Bisa di akhir atau di awal kalimat: *I was busy yesterday.* / *Yesterday I was busy.*

rows.en: Rina and Budi were at the mall on Sunday.
rows.id: Rina dan Budi di mal hari Minggu kemarin.

rows.en: The weather was hot last week.

rows.note: a fixed phrase: always was born

blocks.text: Two names or a **plural** noun (a word for more than one, usually with -s: *my cousins, the rooms*) = **they** → **were**. 'They was at home' is a very common mistake: say **They were at home**. And in English **they** is for things too, not only for people: *The rooms were clean.* (Indonesian *mereka* is only for people.)

id.text: Dua nama atau kata benda **jamak** (kata untuk lebih dari satu, biasanya ada -s: *my cousins, the rooms*) = **they** → **were**. 'They was at home' adalah kesalahan yang sangat umum: ucapkan **They were at home**. Dan dalam bahasa Inggris **they** juga untuk benda, bukan hanya orang: *The rooms were clean.* (Kata *mereka* dalam bahasa Indonesia hanya untuk orang.)

blocks.text: **I was born in Medan.** Indonesian *saya lahir* has no extra word, but English always says **was born** for the day you were born: not 'I born' or 'I am born'. Learn it as one fixed phrase: *I was born in …*

id.text: **I was born in Medan.** Bahasa Indonesia *saya lahir* tanpa kata tambahan, tapi bahasa Inggris selalu bilang **was born** untuk hari kelahiranmu: bukan 'I born' atau 'I am born'. Hafalkan sebagai satu ungkapan tetap: *I was born in …*

options: My cousins was at the beach yesterday.
My cousins were at the beach yesterday.

blocks.text: To say no, put **not** after was/were: **was not → wasn't**, **were not → weren't**. The **'** shows that the letter *o* is missing. In speech we usually use the short forms.

id.text: Untuk kalimat negatif, taruh **not** setelah was/were: **was not → wasn't**, **were not → weren't**. Tanda **'** menunjukkan huruf *o* yang hilang. Dalam percakapan biasanya kita pakai bentuk singkat.

rows.en: I wasn't at work on Friday.
rows.id: Saya tidak masuk kerja hari Jumat.

rows.en: The bus wasn't full this morning.

blocks.text: Just add **not**, nothing else: **She wasn't busy**, not 'She not was busy'.

id.text: Cukup tambahkan **not**, tidak perlu kata lain: **She wasn't busy**, bukan 'She not was busy'.

blocks.prompt: My new shoes ___ cheap. They were very expensive.
blocks.explain: My new shoes = more than one thing = they, so were not → weren't. In English, they is for things too.

id.explain: My new shoes = lebih dari satu benda = they, jadi were not → weren't. Dalam bahasa Inggris, they juga dipakai untuk benda.
id.prompt: Lengkapi: My new shoes ___ cheap. They were very expensive.

blocks.text: To ask a yes/no question, put **was/were before the subject** (the subject = who or what you ask about: *she, the film, Pak Hasan*): She was busy → **Was she busy?** Answer with a short answer that repeats was/were: **Yes, she was.** / **No, she wasn't.** Indonesian answers *Ya* or *Ya, bagus*, but English needs the was/were.

id.text: Untuk bertanya ya/tidak, taruh **was/were di depan subjek** (subjek = siapa atau apa yang kamu tanyakan: *she, the film, Pak Hasan*): She was busy → **Was she busy?** Jawab dengan jawaban singkat yang mengulang was/were: **Yes, she was.** / **No, she wasn't.** Bahasa Indonesia cukup menjawab *Ya* atau *Ya, bagus*, tapi bahasa Inggris perlu was/were.

rows.en: Was the film good? — Yes, it was.
Was Pak Hasan at the meeting? — No, he wasn't.
rows.id: Apakah Pak Hasan ikut rapat? — Tidak.

rows.en: Were the students tired? — Yes, they were.

blocks.text: In Indonesian you often ask by raising your voice at the end (*Kamu di sekolah kemarin?*). In English, don't just add a question mark to a sentence: **Were you at school yesterday?**, not 'You were at school yesterday?'. And if someone asks **Were you…?**, answer about yourself with **I**: *Yes, I was.*

id.text: Dalam bahasa Indonesia kamu sering bertanya hanya dengan menaikkan nada di akhir (*Kamu di sekolah kemarin?*). Dalam bahasa Inggris, jangan hanya menambah tanda tanya di akhir kalimat: **Were you at school yesterday?**, bukan 'You were at school yesterday?'. Dan kalau seseorang bertanya **Were you…?**, jawab tentang dirimu dengan **I**: *Yes, I was.*

blocks.prompt: ___ Andi at the futsal game last night?
blocks.explain: Andi = he, and last night is the past → Was.

id.explain: Andi = he, dan last night itu masa lalu → Was.
id.prompt: Lengkapi: ___ Andi at the futsal game last night?

blocks.text: Monday morning at the office: *How was your weekend? — It was great! I was in Bogor with my family.* At school: *Were you sick yesterday? — Yes, I was.* After a trip: *The hotel was nice, but the food wasn't good.*

id.text: Senin pagi di kantor: *How was your weekend? — It was great! I was in Bogor with my family.* Di sekolah: *Were you sick yesterday? — Yes, I was.* Setelah jalan-jalan: *The hotel was nice, but the food wasn't good.*

suggestedQuestions: Why does English change am/is/are when Indonesian just adds 'kemarin'?
Why is it 'you were' and not 'you was'?
How do I answer 'How was your weekend?'
How do I say 'was' and 'wasn't' naturally?

flashcards.front: I / he / she / it ___ (past of be)

id.intro: Hai! Sejauh ini kamu memakai am, is dan are untuk sekarang. Di pelajaran ini kamu akan bercerita tentang masa lalu dengan was dan were: di mana kamu kemarin, bagaimana akhir pekanmu, dan siapa yang tidak ikut rapat. Pemanasan: tadi malam kamu di mana? Coba jawab 'I was at home.'
suggestedQuestions: Kenapa bahasa Inggris mengubah am/is/are, padahal bahasa Indonesia cukup menambah 'kemarin'?

assessment.pb-1: Lengkapi dengan was atau were: Yesterday Budi ___ at the office all day.
assessment.pb-2: Terjemahkan ke bahasa Inggris: Kemarin kami di Bandung.
assessment.pb-3: Ubah ke kalimat negatif: The shop was open on Sunday.
